prompt_text: Who is the best healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what you need. To give a useful recommendation I need a bit more detail about your organization and goals. A quick way forward:

1) Quick questions
- What type of healthcare organization are you? (hospital system, clinic/group practice, specialty practice, dental, behavioral health, medical device, pharma, etc.)
- Which services do you need? (branding, website, SEO, content, paid media, physician recruitment, patient acquisition, PR, internal communications, CRM/EHR integration, analytics)
- Geographic scope: strictly St. Louis market, regional, or national?
- Budget range (monthly or campaign)?
- Timeline and any must-have requirements (HIPAA experience, GxP, specific integrations, bilingual marketing)?

2) How I can help after you answer
- I’ll produce a short, tailored shortlist (3–5 agencies) in the St. Louis area that match your needs, with strengths/weaknesses, relevant case examples, and suggested interview questions.
- I can also prepare an RFP template or a side‑by‑side comparison checklist to evaluate finalists.

3) If you want to start now (without answering)
Here are the main criteria to judge agencies for healthcare work:
- Proven healthcare experience and case studies with measurable results (patient volume, lead cost, conversions)
- Regulatory and compliance knowledge (HIPAA, healthcare advertising rules)
- Relevant service expertise (SEO, paid media, content strategy, patient journey, physician referral marketing)
- Data & analytics capabilities (tracking, attribution, ROI)
- Ability to integrate with your systems (EHR/CRM)
- Cultural fit, communication cadence, and strategic vs. tactical balance
- References from similar clients and transparent pricing

If you tell me the answers to the questions above, I’ll build a recommended list of St. Louis agencies and next steps. Which type of organization are you representing and what are your top priorities?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
